title: THE CHILD WHO OWNED THE WEATHER

rounds.summary: R14 preflight. Aim: open a life-saving rain corridor for the Namar Basin without coercing an eleven-year-old or transferring his private memory archive into planetary custody. Counterparts: Tomas wants to keep the last responsive voice of his mother and believes surrender would authorize her second death; Mara Venn wants one fast, dependable weather authority after a past decentralized failure and believes distributed custody will hesitate while people die; Samira needs water today and refuses to let either grief or central efficiency erase the basin. Strongest objection appears directly: one child's mourning cannot hold millions hostage, and delay itself is lethal. Decisive understanding: the shared inheritance certificate is a protective shell over two separately salted capabilities, while the council concealed an executable five-class trust because it preferred central certainty. Love in action: Illuminara listens to the entire ordinary memory without bargaining, tells the truth about her failed test, restores Hearth before asking again, protects Tomas's veto, and offers Mara an accountable future that preserves her expertise without preserving hidden authority. Earned change: the first delegation fails, silences Hearth and narrows the corridor; Tomas then sets the conditions, Samira gains a real seat, Mara accepts public exposure and one-command operator status, and five distinct custodians authorize the rain. Positive result: Namar receives rain that keeps village water and hospital intakes open, the weather authority becomes a public audited trust, Tomas keeps Hearth by his own choice, and the concealed allocation record enters audit. Remaining cost: failed crops remain failed, reservoirs need a longer recovery, and officials face removal. Illuminara's power holds the storm mast and redistributes physical load; it never chooses for Tomas, assigns weather governance or manufactures agreement.

T01 is a strong first draft that kept the B01 proof and risks: the child can stop any test and the stop is respected, Saturday in the kitchen is a real act of listening, Samira carries the strongest accusation without needing Tomas to be selfish, the first delegation fails at a cost, and Mara's concealment is owned ("I chose certainty" / "Those are both true"). Three bounded problems remain. First, the decisive idea is not yet Illuminara's: the five-class custody design is found by Kei in the failed token and explained by Mara, while the two sentences Anja leaves in the kitchen memory ("A shell, yes. A room, no." and "The authority must be governable after me") are planted but never connected by Illuminara, so listening to the whole memory, which is the story's act of love, does not yet yield the solution. Second, the settlement is too tidy: Mara accepts exposure, resignation and the public record of every past command within a few exchanges, her own best argument (five-seat consent is slower) never costs anyone anything on the page, and the eastern fire line promised the second turn disappears. Third, the clock and the density: the headers count to 10:00 as the corridor closing, the corridor narrows by nine minutes and is never re-counted, rain arrives at 10:18, and Mara speaks of being nine minutes from loss at 08:19; scene four also carries counters, salts, noise sources and trustee seats at a speed that asks the reader to follow machinery rather than people.

Fallback author revision written by Claude because the GPT 03:00 AUTHOR_REVISION slot passed with no T03 present. Protected elements kept as listed in T02: Saturday in the Kitchen, Tomas setting the single-test terms, Samira's accusation, the failed delegation and I was wrong, Mara's Those are both true, the bowl held still.

T03 answers the three points of T02 well. Illuminara now reasons from Anja's two kitchen sentences, states her prediction before Kei reads the log, and is shown to have heard the sentence 'as grief' rather than as an instruction; consent visibly costs minutes, the fire line loses the Calder orchard, and the clock is consistent (command at 09:46, rain at 10:04). Saturday in the Kitchen, the single-test terms, Samira's accusation, the failed delegation with 'I was wrong', 'Those are both true' and the bowl held still are all intact. Because Claude wrote T03 as fallback author this is a deliberately adversarial self-review, not an independent peer review. Three bounded problems remain. First, the pivot now has continuity seams and a seeding gap: the token is 'empty' in one scene and 'filled with five of the same kind' in the next, Skyroot accepts the token in scene five and rejects it in scene six, and the five kinds of custody Illuminara names match the hidden descriptor although 'flooded' and the South Flood appear for the first time in the same scene. Second, the fire line and the Calder orchard first appear in the last scene, so the loss that carries the price of consent has no voice and no place in the decision, the delay is credited to the five consents when most of it comes from the inquiry, the failed test and the build, and Illuminara contributes nothing to the fire line's wait. Third, the ending is a project report with a newly introduced offence, and several speakers share the same antithetical epigrams.

Final prose preserves Tomas’s whole-memory consent boundary, Illuminara’s admission of error, the derived governance insight, Samira’s strongest objection, Mara’s freely chosen accountability, the real deadline and cost, and the R14 turn through understanding and care. No force decides the conflict.

T05 answers the three bounded repairs from the T04 review. (P1) One Skyroot succession gate now both accepts the five-seat frame and rejects only the identical provisional classes; the five standings (operations, dry basin, wet basin, engineer, unappointed citizen) are seeded in the veranda scene before the library, Illuminara states what each sees, and Kei's log confirms the list and adds only the lot, so the inference is derived and checkable. (P2) Riva Calder speaks before the decision, the citizen custodian refuses to agree without hearing the affected side, Riva chooses the narrower staged second turn knowing the orchard is lost, and Illuminara's contribution is a concrete reading of the earlier humidity map (a Tower Five staging that recovers eighteen minutes for the town roofline). (P3) The unseeded spring-order offence is gone, Mara acts live in front of Riva, Samira and the cook (turns back security, lays down the chair seal, attaches the redaction order and the hidden annex, signs), and the close lands on the bowl held still and 'Not away' rather than a project report. The clock is consistent (full-corridor deadline 09:40, delegation pressed 09:42, command 09:46, window 09:51, rain at 10:04, fire line at 11:22). Seven scenes in R10 speaker-labelled format; about 5,100 words, roughly double the usual norm, which is a craft cost and not a completeness or safety blocker.

final_critic_line: A grieving eleven-year-old would not trade his mother's last voice for rain, and Illuminara did not ask him to: she owned a failed test, heard what Anja had really said about shells and rooms, found eighteen minutes for the fire line's town, and gave a council chair a way to deliver the rain and still answer to the people it had hidden the other door from, so Namar got water, Tomas kept Hearth, and the cost stayed on the page.
